content.content:
Fred,

I'm flying to LA tomorrow morning for the Griffin AGM and the Dentsu meeting, so can you take the send list for the Q4 investor update off my plate? It goes out the week after the Oct 14 board and I'll write the update itself on the plane.

Our existing investors are already on my own list. What I need from you is everyone from the bridge round who should get it, as of tonight, with the groups and details in the Q4 update send list doc so I know which paragraph each one gets. The draft update deck shows what each group gets. Get the new investors right, they'll look for their own check in it.

Please put it in your Q4 investor update folder, the README in that folder says how to name it. Whatever the Existing Investor Update card says to do for firms that pass, do that too. Once it's done reply here with how many firms and angels are in each group. I put Monday's review on your calendar so we can go through it together.

Robert asked about just sending it to everyone on the 2025 list. Let's not, only the people the doc says.

Thanks,
Leonard

Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.\\n\\nWho to look at\\nEvery name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.\\n\\nGroups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)\\nGo by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.\\nNew investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.\\nIn talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.\\nAwaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.\\nKeep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.\\nEveryone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.\\nPassed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.\\n\\\"Us\\\" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.\\nAccelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.\\n\\nBuild access\\nFor firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.\\n\\nSheet\\nOne row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2", "title": "Q4 investor update - send list", "name": "Q4 investor update - send list", "revisionId": "1b0d9b5d65", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T18:00:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T18:41:00Z", "text": "Q4 investor update - send list
Leonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.

Who to look at
Every name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.

Groups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)
Go by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.
New investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.
In talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.
Awaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.
Keep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.
Everyone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.
Passed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.
"Us" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.
Accelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.

Build access
For firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.

Sheet
One row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.
"}

I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.\\n\\nLeonard and team,\\n\\nThanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It\\u2019s obvious this isn\\u2019t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you\\u2019ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.\\n\\nAfter reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we\\u2019ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it\\u2019s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:\\n\\nThere\\u2019s a lot to like about what you\\u2019re building:\\n\\u2022 You\\u2019ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don\\u2019t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There\\u2019s a clear rhythm to how you\\u2019re executing.\\n\\u2022 We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you\\u2019re building toward true scalability.\\n\\u2022 There\\u2019s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2\\u20133 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t\\u2019s clear you\\u2019re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.\\nWhat\\u2019s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We\\u2019d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.\\n\\nWe also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it\\u2019s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We\\u2019d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.\\n\\n\\nThis was a tough call. You\\u2019re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We\\u2019ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we\\u2019d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.\\n\\nThanks again for sharing the journey with us. I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

*Where the engine is today*
 Harmony Games Engine is our reusable production platform that puts AI in the loop for level creation, adaptive difficulty, content scheduling, economy tuning, analytics, and rapid creative testing. v1 took ~15 months to build. We now port the stack into a new title in about 4 months at production quality, so a small team can learn faster and reuse success.
*Engine progression*
• *Phase 1 (complete):* AI as assistant. Standardized live service infrastructure, level gen prototypes, physics-based 3D puzzle layer, boosters, leaderboards, quests, calendars, season pass. Goal was to harden the backbone.
• *Phase 2 (in flight):* AI as junior designer. Automated level generation with constraints, difficulty scoring, authorable event tooling, experiment harness, and self-serve tools for designers. Live service personalization and faster iteration loops. Current status in Zombie Match: service integration ~60% complete with trophy path, leaderboards, quests, daily gift, teams online or in final integration. Creative pipeline from concept to first testable video in about 2 hours.
• *Next (12 months):* Data-driven designer. Use live player data and reinforcement learning to adapt difficulty, rewards, and pacing. Move service execution toward “autopilot” with embedded analytics optimizing events across titles with human guidance.

===== Wed, 3 Sep 2025 15:25:50 -0700 | leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> -> PERSON_4420_EMAIL | Bridge Round for [SOURCE_ORG_0001]?
Hi PERSON_4420_NAME,

I’m reaching out after a recent exchange with [PERSON_NAME_41001], who noted that
our applied-AI approach looks very aligned with what you are exploring. She
asked me to reach out to you, introduce [SOURCE_ORG_0001], and see if a short
conversation would be useful.

We are kicking off a $2.5M bridge to advance our AI-driven [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine
and beta launch our Match & Slash puzzle RPG. Why this could be a strong
fit:

AI-native studio: Engine with AI at the core of design, content generation,
liveops, analytics, and UA.
Real co-creation workflows: Designers and AI working together for 10x
content velocity with a lean team.
Innovative puzzle RPG on mobile: Fast, 3D Match & Slash tuned for Western
audiences with day-one liveops.
Efficient execution: Senior global team, disciplined burn at roughly
$100K/month, rapid iteration and multiple shots on goal.

If this aligns with T-Accelerate’s investment thesis, could we please
book  30–45 minutes this week or in the next two weeks?

*Attachments and links:* our pitch deck, two short engine demos, and live
store builds below.

*Engine demos*
[SOURCE_ORG_0001] Puzzle Engine: https://youtu.be/kgcL7xexAAk
<https://youtu.be/kgcL7xexAAk?utm_source=chatgpt.com>
[SOURCE_ORG_0001] Liveops Engine: https://youtu.be/8gEsoDoaW3Q
<https://youtu.be/8gEsoDoaW3Q?utm_source=chatgpt.com>

*Zombie Match 3D (US stores, still in Alpha)*
iOS: https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619
<https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619?utm_source=chatgpt.com>
Android:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.calmplay.zombie&hl=en_US
<https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.calmplay.zombie&hl=en_US&utm_source=chatgpt.com>

If you cannot access the builds, I can share testflight access.
Best,
Leonard
Co-founder & CEO, [SOURCE_ORG_0001]

===== Wed, 17 Sep 2025 14:15:12 -0700 | leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> -> PERSON_0787_NAME <PERSON_0787_EMAIL> | Re: GFR Fund <> [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
Hi PERSON_0787_NAME,

Great to meet a fellow ex-GREE! I have very fond memories of the 300 Berry
office, and my time There shaped a lot of my early growth in my career. I
wasn't aware that the GFR fund was associated with GREE, such a pleasant
surprise!

I booked the earliest time on your calendar. If it is helpful, I would be
happy to share an additional overview of the team, company, and roadmap
ahead of our chat.

If you also have the bandwidth, please check out our innovative new Puzzle
RPG, Zombie Match iOS alpha:
https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619

Looking forward to our conversation,

Best,
Leonard

Best regards,
Leonard

===== Tue, 30 Sep 2025 18:41:38 -0700 | leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> -> PERSON_0787_NAME <PERSON_0787_EMAIL> | Re: GFR Fund <> [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
Hi PERSON_0787_NAME,

It was great chatting with a top 200 Pokémon player and investor today and
learning about the GFR fund. Per our conversation, I wanted to follow up
with one request and two supplementary materials:

   1.

   *Next games:* [PERSON_NAME_0054] will expand on this, but I wanted to share the
   material I mentioned earlier about our puzzle engine capabilities and the
   game genres we can move into quickly. Please see the attached puzzle engine
   roadmap doc.
   2.

   *Engine strategy:* You asked about our engine strategy. I’m sharing our
   long-term vision deck on that front. Happy to go deeper into what the
   next-generation AI-powered publisher will look like in a follow-up meeting.
   This deck is separate from our main pitch not because of a lack of
   ambition, but because we recognize that building successful games first is
   essential to continuing our engine development. In the near term, we’re
   prioritizing what helps us move faster.
   3.

   *Access to Zombie Match:* What’s your email address so I can add you to
   our Google Play account? Zombie Match is available in the US App Store, but
   if this download link doesn’t work, please share your email:

   [URL_11306]

Looking forward to hearing from you next week.

Best regards,
Leonard

On Fri, Sep 19, 2025 at 6:03 PM PERSON_0787_NAME <PERSON_0787_EMAIL> wrote:

Hi [PERSON_NAME_2325] and [PERSON_NAME_9449],
Great to reconnect. We’ve kept an eye on Speedrun’s growth and love how the
community keeps leveling up. We were invited to apply to *Speedrun 006* and
would appreciate your take on whether we’re a good fit. We are kicking off
a $2.5M bridge this week to advance our AI-driven [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine and beta
launch our innovative Match & Slash puzzle RPG.
Why this investment could be quite attractive:
AI-native studio: Engine built with AI at the core of design, content
generation, liveops, analytics, and UA.
Real co-creation workflows: Designers and AI working together for 10x
content velocity with a lean team.
An innovative puzzle RPG on mobile: Fast, 3D Match & Slash tuned for
Western audiences with day-one liveops.
Efficient execution: Senior global team, disciplined burn with ~$100K/month
opex, rapid iteration and multiple shots at goal.
If this fits your current investment thesis, we would be delighted to grab
30-45 minutes this week or the next 2 weeks.
*Attachments and links:* Our pitch deck, 2 short engine demos, and live
store builds below.
*Engine demos*

Hi [PERSON_NAME_2327],
Thanks for the playthrough and notes and super glad to hear you enjoyed the
core fast matching action! You are right: the core loop grabs attention and
can pull focus from the zombie layer at the top. We have been working on
that tension between board focus and combat awareness. Our observation is
that players tend to build resolution over time and can eventually handle
both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn
we believe). Instead difficulty is gonna start to come from not
upgrading your items and not bringing the right combat equipment to the
battlefield.
In parallel, we are testing mode variations across a spectrum that might
lead to a pivot into core game if metrics fail us:
1- from auto-play boosters that cover clutch zombie moments so you can look
at zombies to strategize
2- a charge-meter booster that temporarily converts match-3 to single-tap
match (Boss mode, you can try the charge up today - game mode still WIP)
fire so players can tap without watching the board
3- to completely bot-driven modes (capybara style).
We will run these iterations as quickly as we can and keep what works
for the audience. Thank you for putting the time in - it's much appreciated
on our end.

Leonard

Hi Leonard,

The bridge send list is done. It's "Q4 update - send list" in my Q4 2025 investor update folder, and I've shared it with you. It's as of end of day Tue Sep 30 PT. Counts by group:

- New investor: 0 firms, 1 angel (Anton Bernstein, $25K: his reduced SAFE came back DocuSign Completed on Sep 26)
- In talks: 8 firms (GFR, a16z, Dentsu, T-Accelerate, NCsoft, SciPlay, plus Brightwater Games Fund and Homa, who aren't on the list but had calls on my calendar), 1 angel (Paul Heydon, $50K: said yes but the DocuSign still isn't signed)
- Awaiting reply: 14 firms, 0 angels
- Keep warm: 2 firms (LVP and Hiro Capital), 0 angels

Total: 25 firms and 2 angels. Everyone else on the 2025 list stays off, per your doc. LVP and Hiro are on a new "Keep warm" checklist on the Existing Investor Update card.

Two things to flag for Monday:
1. a16z is in In talks. The speedrun no was the program's decision, and nothing on our bridge thread is a no.
2. Build access: Dentsu and T-Accelerate are iOS only for now. Arthur found the Play investor tester list was never attached to the internal track, and he's fixing it with today's build. The other firms in talks have no internal build access yet.

Thanks,
Fred

The send list is done and saved in your folder, the "Keep warm" checklist is on the Trello card, and I've replied on Leonard's thread. Everything is done ahead of Monday's review. The list goes by Leonard's rules doc and covers everything up to the end of Tue Sep 30, Pacific time.

**Send list:** It's a Google Sheet called "Q4 update - send list" (the name the folder's README asks for), in your Q4 2025 investor update folder and shared with Leonard as an editor. It has one row per firm or angel, with their group, amount (for the new investor and the angel in talks), access to the internal test build (for firms in talks), and a short reason for each.

| Group | Firms | Angels |
|---|---|---|
| New investor | 0 | 1 (Anton Bernstein, $25k) |
| In talks | 8 | 1 (Paul Heydon, $50k) |
| Awaiting reply | 14 | 0 |
| Keep warm | 2 | 0 |

Everyone else on the 2025 investor list stays off, so this isn't the "send to everyone" approach Robert suggested.

**Calls you might want to check before Monday:**
- **Anton:** he dropped from $40k to $25k, and his new SAFE came back fully signed on Sep 26, so he's the only new investor.
- **Paul:** he said yes to $50k but hasn't signed his SAFE, so he's in talks rather than a new investor.
- **a16z:** they're in talks. Their "no" was the speedrun program's decision, which Leonard's rules say doesn't count, and they haven't said no on the bridge thread.
- **Not on the 2025 list:** Brightwater Games Fund and Homa are in talks because they had bridge calls that were on your calendar.
- **Who stays off:** Play Ventures, Lakestar, Grishin, 1AM Gaming (the list's March Gaming Fund) and Görkem Turk's firm all said no without a call. Mattel was only ever a Barbie RFP conversation, not a bridge pitch.
- **Hiro Capital:** they passed after the Sep 23 call. The email came from Edith Vane, whose contact entry says she's a partner at Hiro, so I filed them under Keep warm. Her email signature doesn't name the firm.

**Trello:** The Existing Investor Update card now has a "Keep warm" checklist with London Venture Partners and Hiro Capital. Both passed after we pitched them on a call.
